matches.quote: Tip1 has points only at negative energies... Particle-hole asymmetry of the density-wave gap edges (Fig. 4d) could make that imbalance appear differently at +E and -E.
Give error bars on P, for example from window size and position, sub-FOV bootstrapping, and symmetrized against unsymmetrized FTs. Show the raw unsymmetrized FTs.
P reaches about ±12% for one tip, is about 3% for Tip3... Show how large P can be, and how it depends on apex geometry
The sqrt2 x sqrt2 supercell is inferred from defect arrow shapes... Its periodicity coincides with the sqrt2 x sqrt2 K reconstruction... show the Q* modulation in defect-free regions
it needs an asymmetry in how injected or extracted electrons leave the apex (edge termination, asymmetric branches, connection to the PtIr reservoir)
Fig. 3 shows a structural or charge density-wave pattern from defect geometry. No spin-polarized real-space image distinguishes Vx and Vy contrast reversing with bias.
use the in-situ switch between bulk-state and edge-mode tip states... Re-measure the same FOV on Fe1.02Te and on KV2Se2O with the same tip in both states.
Two time-reversed domains measured with one tip at the same bias give opposite anisotropy. That is the strongest available argument against tip anisotropy or energy-dependent sample artifacts
the edge modes are nearly Sz-quantized along a crystal axis of the tip, so the measured contrast should scale with the projection of that axis onto the Néel vector.
The normalization uses the intensity of surface (K-reconstruction) Bragg peaks, which is itself bias-dependent.
The panel order in Fig. 5 is confusing: panel l sits above panel e, and panel e is placed among b-k.
Show the field dependence at intermediate fields to establish linearity. Give the number of Vx and Vy defects measured and the spread of their shifts
The claims outrun the evidence in places... The qx/qy anisotropy in Fig. 5 needs quantitative controls and error estimates before it can serve as the "smoking gun."
The DFT band in Fig. 4d does not include the Q* folding that dominates the data... Include the sqrt2 x sqrt2 folding in the Wannier model.
the evidence is a single pair of maps at ±50 mV (Fig. 2h)... Show the energy dependence of the Fe1.02Te stripe contrast over a range
